subject: MAP: Orchard Health — Post-signature implementation plan and canary schedule
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchardhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Orchard Health — Post-signature implementation plan and canary schedule

Hi Sarah / team,

Congrats again on the signature — excited to get moving. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation timeline, evaluation gates, and training cadence. High-level ask: please confirm the proposed canary window and your go/no-go criteria so we can lock resource reservations.

Snapshot (proposed):
- Week 0 (kickoff): Project kickoff call, access & account provisioning, SSO & KMS check.
- Week 1–2 (canary): Small cohort (10% traffic), monitored for latency, failure rate, and 1k prompt evaluation set.
- Week 3–4 (migration): Gradual traffic ramp + parallel validation; rollback guardrails in place.
- Week 5 (training): Ops + developer training sessions (2 x 90 min) + runbooks handed off.
- Week 6 (GO-LIVE): Full cutover and 30-day monitoring window.

Canary success criteria (suggested):
- P95 latency under 220ms for standard prompt mix
- Error rate < 0.5% (5xx / client errors)
- Quality: pass on 95% of the evaluation prompt set (we'll validate with your SMEs)

Attachments: Orchard_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP + timeline + owner matrix), training-plan.pptx (agenda), canary-checklist.xlsx (initial checklist).

Please reply with any date constraints or mandatory blackout windows on your side. If the timeline looks tight we can shift the canary start.

Next steps from us once you confirm dates:
- Finalize resource reservation (Dedicated pool and SLO targets)
- Share canary test prompts and evaluation rubric
- Book training sessions and invite lists

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Rachel — this looks comprehensive and appreciate the clarity. A couple of asks from our side:

- Can we push the canary start two weeks later? Our compliance team needs an additional review of the data retention controls and they'd like a buffer.
- Training: prefer sessions in the early morning (PST) and would like one session recorded for the wider ops team.
- For the evaluation rubric, can you include a brief mapping to our internal acceptance test ids (I will share a list).

If that's acceptable we'll route the MAP to procurement for a final nod and confirm PO timeline. For now tentatively holding the week-of Aug 6 for canary start.

Thanks Sarah — pushing the canary two weeks is fine on our side; we should shift the entire schedule accordingly. Proposed adjusted windows below (tentative):
- Kickoff: Jul 26 (account setup + SSO smoke tests)
- Canary: Aug 6–Aug 19 (2-week window, start with internal traffic, then invite selected pilot clinics)
- Migration ramp: Aug 20–Sep 2
- Training: Sep 3–Sep 9 (2 instructor-led sessions + 1 office hours)
- Go-live: Sep 10

Marissa notes: we will need a named SME from Orchard for prompt evaluation and a sandbox dataset for baseline metrics. Vivek — can your team allocate a small dedicated pool for the canary (2 x T4 equivalent) and enable prefix-KV caching for pilot prompts? I attached an internal playbook link and the canary checklist draft for visibility.

Subject: Re: MAP: Orchard Health — Post-signature implementation plan and canary schedule

Thanks — confirmed we can reserve a small dedicated pool for the canary: 2x A100-similar vCPU/GPU equivalents (we'll translate to customers as "dedicated pilot capacity"). Technical notes for the canary checklist:

- KV/prefix caching: enable for the pilot prompt set (reduces cold-start token delta). We'll whitelist prompts provided by Orchard to protect cached content.
- Monitoring hooks: we will stream token-level latency metrics to the shared project dashboard; set alert thresholds at P95 > 250ms and error rate > 0.5%.
- Fallback policy: automatic reroute to a lower-capacity variant if latency spikes > 300ms for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Data handling: logs retained per agreed KMS policy and only aggregated telemetry passed to Redwood analytics unless otherwise approved.

I attached the canary-checklist.xlsx (draft) with step-by-step run tasks and test ids mapped to our evaluation harness.
